text: Derive the expected NVMe bytes per token for a 40-layer top-8 MoE under hit rate h (uniform across layers): bytes = 320*(1-h)*expert_bytes (+ speculative waste term). Plug expert_bytes 1.5 MiB INT4 and 0.75 MiB 2-bit. At B=400,45,21 MB/s compute ideal I/O ms/token ignoring overlap. Show steps and state assumptions.

Define precision@8 and recall@8/12/16 for expert prediction per layer and pooled. A predictor emits ranked (layer, expert, confidence). With 256 experts and 8 true per layer, what does random achieve? Work a tiny numeric example with 2 layers and show how confidence thresholds trade bytes wasted vs misses avoided.

State Belady/MIN optimality for a fixed trace and capacity. Prove by exchange argument that evicting the farthest-next-use expert never hurts. Explain why it is a ceiling (needs future knowledge) and how to brute-force it on tiny traces to validate a simulator.

Model per-layer hit-rate curves H_l(c) from calibration. Formalize the slot-allocation problem: maximize sum of gains subject to sum c_l = C. Show greedy by delta-H is optimal for concave curves and can fail otherwise; give the 8-block pathology example and the lookahead remedy intuition. No implementation, just math.

An always-wrong predictor with R1-R3 on (speculative held in software queue, device cap one tile, speculate-only-when-idle) must add at most cap/B + t_req to any exact miss. Prove the bound and explain how to measure max and P95 added delay on real traces. Include median and mean comparison and why both matter under skew.

Quantify the output-head cost: 509M params, BF16 1 GB vs INT4 250 MB RAM read per token. At 10 sustained GOPS for compute plus measured RAM bandwidth X, when is the head vs the expert stage dominant? Derive the crossover and list what to measure on-device before trusting tok/s.

Define reuse-distance distribution per layer for 10240 layer-qualified experts over decode tokens. Relate stack distance to hit rate under LRU for a given capacity. Sketch how to compute it from traces in O(tokens*layers) and how non-stationarity across domains shows up in the curves.
